archetypes.name: wire-contracts
archetypes.rationale: The migration ports 20+ CLI verbs with strict KV/TSV/NDJSON output contracts; subtle field-order, exit-code, or conditional-emission drift will silently break orchestration callers that parse stdout positionally.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review every new Python CLI verb for exact wire-contract fidelity against the retired shell scripts described in the plan: KV key names and emission order, TSV column order and empty-field placeholders, NDJSON field sets (including backward-compat aliases like `self_deploying_gap`), phase-conditional key emission (especially `promote-latest` pre- vs post-selection phases), and exit codes for normal vs usage-error vs partial-failure paths. Pay particular attention to `resolve-prs` six-key stdout ordering, `map-runs` no-header TSV column stability, `close-priors` TAB-separated `CLOSE_FAILED` rows, and `pacific-timestamp` no-stdout behavior on parse failure. Flag any Python implementation that emits keys in a different order, omits conditional keys, or returns a different exit code than documented in the plan. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: quiet-routing
archetypes.rationale: The fd-3 quiet stream (emit/emit_kv, LARCH_QUIET_ACTIVE inheritance) is a cross-cutting runtime contract; a regression in plugin read-version or any migrated helper silently swallows stdout from command-substitution callers.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every migrated Python module for correct quiet-mode routing: verify that `plugin read-version` calls `logging_util.quiet_init` before emitting `LARCH_PLUGIN_VERSION`, that inherited `LARCH_QUIET_ACTIVE` state does not suppress stdout captured by command substitution in shell callers, and that the fd-3 quiet stream contract from `scripts/lib-quiet.md` is preserved where shipped callers depend on `emit`/`emit_kv` semantics. Check that `promote` human-facing messages still route through quiet mode while KV output goes to stdout, and that `release finish` and `release prepare` do not inadvertently emit human-readable messages on stdout where callers expect only KV pairs. Flag any module that emits human text to stdout where only KV output is expected, or that fails to reinitialize quiet routing in a subprocess context. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: cli-registry
archetypes.rationale: The cli.py lazy-import registry maps 20+ domain/verb pairs; a single typo, wrong function reference, or import-time side effect in a new module will silently fail all callers for that verb.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit `python/cli.py` to verify that every domain/verb pair listed in the plan (release classify-bump, release prepare, release set-version, release finish, release promote, release promote-latest, plugin read-version, verify main, audit-runs preflight through close-priors, combine-issues fetch/apply, analyze-issues fetch/run/analyze/render-chart) is registered with the correct module path and function name, and that no new module is imported at the top level (lazy-import-only constraint). Check each new Python module for import-time side effects (global state mutations, file I/O, subprocess calls at module scope) that would break the lazy-import guarantee. Verify the stdlib-only constraint: no third-party packages in any new module, confirmed by inspecting import statements. Flag missing verb registrations, wrong function names, or any top-level import of a new module in cli.py. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
